game.name: CubeCraft Parkour
game.rules:
General ruleset:

• Submissions must be recorded on the CubeCraft Games network on the most up-to-date version of the track.

• Video footage is required for all submissions. Any video sharing platform may be used within reason, but the video must be publicly accessible.

• Irrelevant footage visible before the start of the submitted run must be limited to a maximum of 10 seconds. (A.K.A. get to the run quickly, please) Besides editing, players can also satisfy this rule by using a timestamped link that takes the viewer directly to the beginning of the run. This can be done on many video sharing platforms by navigating to the video, clicking "Share", and clicking on the checkbox labelled "Start at [time]".

• Exploitation of bugs or glitches is not permitted during runs. This includes jumping on the edge of a block that would usually restart the player.

• The in-game timer must remain clearly visible at all times, and cropping / blurring / covering parts of the screen is strongly discouraged. Runs may get rejected if deemed too obscure. Rejections for this rule are at the discretion of the staff team.

• The use of advantageous in-game modifiers (such as speed) is not allowed.

• Runs may be rejected if the timer takes too long to begin counting at the start of a level, as this is due to lag and can cause the timer to display a quicker time than it is supposed to.

• Bedrock runs that use the strategy of starting immediately after dying should include a couple seconds of said death.

This is the general ruleset that applies to all runs. Make sure you also consult the rules for your chosen category (IL run, entire run, etc.) before submitting a run.

categories.name: Simple [JE] / Easy [BE] (Old) (Archived 12/23/24)
categories.rules:
This is the ruleset for entire game runs. Make sure to read our general ruleset as well if you haven't already.

Entire Game Run Ruleset:

• The goal for entire game runs is to complete every level in the chosen difficulty.

• The levels must be completed back to back with no cuts in the video.

• Levels can be completed in any order.

• For entire game runs, we use an external tool to determine the time of a submission. The tool we use can be found here: slashinfty.github.io/yt-frame-timer. We are required to insert two video endpoints that represent the beginning and end of the run. For the starting frame, we use the last frame that the timer shows "0:000". For the ending frame, we use the moment the last level completion text pops up. The tool will then calculate the exact time of the submission.

categories.name: Entire
categories.rules:
This is the ruleset for entire runs. Make sure to read our general ruleset as well if you haven't already.

For Competitive Levels: Competitive levels share the column for entire runs, but are unrelated. For these runs, just follow the general and IL rules.

Entire Run Ruleset:

• The goal for an entire run is to complete every level in the chosen map.

• The levels must be completed back-to-back with no cuts in the video.

• Levels can be completed in any order.

Entire Run Timing:

• For entire runs, we use an external frame timer ([https://slashinfty.github.io/yt-frame-timer/](https://slashinfty.github.io/yt-frame-timer/)) to determine the time of a submission. For the starting frame, we use the frame before the timer resets. For the ending frame, we use the moment the last level completion text pops up. The tool will then calculate the exact time of the submission. Try to leave some time in the video before and after the run starts and ends so we have some breathing room during retiming.

•Because our timing method for entire runs requires exact frames, the video platform that the submission uses must allow for precise frame stepping. Youtube is one such platform, though there may be others.

categories.name: Level 1
categories.rules:
This is the ruleset for single level (or IL) runs. Make sure to read our general ruleset as well if you haven't already.

Single level runs:

The goal for single level runs is to beat one level in a chosen map as quickly as possible.

• Videos containing more than one run must have a direct link to the correct time stamp of the submitted run. On Youtube this can be done by navigating to the video, clicking "Share", and clicking on the checkbox labelled "Start at [time]". This method can also be used for videos with only one run to bypass the "Irrelevant footage must be limited to 10 seconds" rule.

• For single level runs, the in-game timer is used to determine the time of a submission. Times will be automatically rounded to the nearest minecraft tick (multiple of 0.050 seconds)
